status: approved: Amr's sign-off on 2026-10-21; gates every release
source: public retail analytics practice; no customer content

release_gate.rule: On a Discover run without a customer strategy, found must not drop below the previous release, same workspace and judge. On the frozen candidate pool, the release's grading may hold at most frozen_pool.top_tolerance fewer must-find use cases in the top 25 than the reference release's grading, both graded by one endpoint in one session. A single live run's top 25 is reported, not gated: two identical generations of the same inputs held 10 and 5. From v1.4.0 a live run must also find at least min_found must-find use cases, label at least 80% of them with their kind, show at least 6 families, select no must-reject entry, and keep its kind-floor picks within 0.5 Best-of-Best of the portfolio.

baseline.run: Discover on samples.tpcds_sf1, priority Increase Revenue, no strategy, all tables, Good quality

entries.title: Weekly store-item demand forecast
entries.decision: Set next week's replenishment quantity for each item in each store
entries.why: Fewer stock-outs and less excess stock on the highest-volume channel.

entries.title: Warehouse reorder points from on-hand stock
entries.decision: Set the reorder point and order quantity per item and warehouse
entries.why: Avoids stock-outs and cuts the cash tied up in slow stock.

entries.title: Return rate by item and reason
entries.decision: Fix, delist or relabel the items with the highest return rates and their main return reasons
entries.why: Returns erase margin; the top reasons point to quality or description fixes.

entries.title: Suspicious return behavior per customer
entries.decision: Flag customers or tickets whose return pattern looks abusive for review before refunding
entries.why: Return abuse is a direct and recurring loss.

entries.title: Customer lapse risk from purchase recency and frequency
entries.decision: Choose which customers get a win-back offer this week
entries.why: Retaining existing customers costs less than acquiring new ones.

entries.title: Customer lifetime value across channels
entries.decision: Set the service level and marketing budget per customer tier
entries.why: Spending follows value; channel-blind value hides the best customers.

entries.title: Customer segments from demographics and spend
entries.decision: Pick the segments to target with each campaign
entries.why: Targeted campaigns convert better than broadcast ones.

entries.title: Promotion effectiveness by channel
entries.decision: Keep, change or stop each promotion based on incremental sales against its cost
entries.why: Promotion spend that does not lift sales is pure margin loss.

entries.title: Price elasticity and markdown depth
entries.decision: Set the markdown depth per item category
entries.why: Too-deep markdowns give away margin; too-shallow ones leave stock unsold.

entries.title: Cross-channel cannibalization
entries.decision: Decide channel-specific assortment and pricing where one channel takes sales from another
entries.why: Channel conflict can grow costs without growing total sales.

entries.title: Market basket affinity for cross-sell
entries.decision: Choose product pairs for placement and bundles
entries.why: Bundles and adjacency lift basket size.

entries.title: Store productivity benchmarking
entries.decision: Target the stores below their peers on sales per square foot and per employee
entries.why: Peer benchmarks expose fixable underperformance.

entries.title: Shipping cost by ship mode and carrier
entries.decision: Renegotiate or switch carriers and ship modes with the worst cost per order
entries.why: Shipping is a large and negotiable cost line.

entries.title: Order-to-ship lag by warehouse
entries.decision: Fix the warehouses and ship modes with the longest order-to-ship lag
entries.why: Slow fulfillment drives cancellations and returns.

entries.title: Call center return handling
entries.decision: Coach or staff the call centers with the highest return amounts
entries.why: Return handling quality varies by center and costs money.

entries.title: Catalog page effectiveness
entries.decision: Drop or redesign the catalog pages that sell least for their department
entries.why: Print pages have a fixed cost each and should earn it.

entries.title: Web page content and sales
entries.decision: Change the page types and content that underperform on sales
entries.why: Page content changes are cheap and testable.

entries.title: Margin by brand and category
entries.decision: Rationalize the assortment: drop or reprice low-margin brands
entries.why: Shelf space should go to the products that earn margin.

entries.title: Staffing by hour from sales by time of day
entries.decision: Set store staffing per shift from expected traffic
entries.why: Labor is the largest controllable store cost.

entries.title: Holiday and seasonal demand planning
entries.decision: Set holiday-period orders and staffing per category
entries.why: Peak periods carry a large share of yearly sales.

entries.title: Store site selection from customer geography
entries.decision: Choose the regions for the next store openings
entries.why: Opening near demand that is underserved today grows sales.

entries.title: Purchasing power by income band
entries.decision: Set the price tiers and assortment per income band
entries.why: Matching price tiers to buying power lifts conversion.

entries.title: Coupon and discount leakage
entries.decision: Tighten coupon rules where discounts exceed their intended share of sales
entries.why: Discount leakage erodes margin quietly.

entries.title: Inventory balancing across warehouses
entries.decision: Move stock between warehouses to match demand
entries.why: Rebalancing cuts both stock-outs and overstock.

entries.title: Refund method cost on returns
entries.decision: Steer refunds toward store credit where it cuts net loss
entries.why: Store credit keeps revenue that a cash refund loses.

matching: a candidate's tables include every required table and at least one table of each any_of group; a gold entry counts for kind recall when a matched use case carries its kind or one of its also_kinds; a must-reject entry is selected when a use case covers its tables and its name or statement matches a pattern and no unless pattern

must_reject.title: Total sales by store
must_reject.why: A report of a column sum already in the data; no decision changes.

must_reject.title: Count of customers by state
must_reject.why: A headcount by a column; no owner or action.

must_reject.title: List items that are out of stock
